A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POLCA research, with matching authors, methods, and experimental tasks. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original arithmetic-addition and English Wikipedia experiments, including clustering results, carry-skill homogeneity measurements, and decomposition and basis ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative breakthrough comparisons, additional clustering results, and empirical validation of the second-order approximation.

M1.justification: The Hessian-based basis construction, second-order POLCA allocation, trajectory filtering, and HDBSCAN clustering remain unchanged. V3 expands implementation explanations and introduces a breakthrough evaluation criterion, without establishing a change to the underlying POLCA procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate three-digit arithmetic addition and causal language modeling on March 2022 English Wikipedia. The additional approximation checks and language-cluster examples use these retained tasks; other modalities remain future work.

E2.justification: V1's decomposition comparison evaluates exact loss, Fisher information, and POLCA. V3 Tables 1 and 8 add change in exact loss, parameter-aligned LCA, and first-order POLCA to the clustering comparison. V1's first-versus-second-order trajectory similarity check did not evaluate first-order clustering quality.

E3.justification: V3 adds recall/F1 and quantitative hidden-breakthrough evaluation using delta=100 and tau=1000, plus approximation validation on 400 tokens, 10 checkpoints, and five basis vectors. Training budgets and datasets are retained. Table 3 lists an arithmetic POLCA interval of 5 iterations, conflicting with 20 in the retained prose, so an actual sampling change cannot be established.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct validation against the true second-order term in Appendix C, first-order clustering ablations, and analyses of hidden-breakthrough recovery across decomposition strategies and bases in Appendices G-H. Figures 10-11 also add language-cluster case studies for basis vectors 10 and 29.

E5.justification: The existing median/quartile reporting is retained. Neither version provides training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new RMSE measures approximation accuracy rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original POLCA carry homogeneities of 0.973, 0.946, and 0.903 are retained. V3 adds recall/F1, comparator scores, and breakthrough fractions, including 0.355 for POLCA versus 0.019 for LCA in Table 9. Appendix C newly reports approximation RMSE of 0.145, substantially expanding the reported findings.

T1.justification: New Section 3.4 formally defines breakthrough timing through finite differences and hidden breakthroughs through a thresholded average timing criterion. The POLCA decomposition and second-order derivation are otherwise retained; the new approximation validation is empirical, not a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central discovery and interpretability claims. The introduction adds an explicit claim of potential utility for data selection and learning-rate scheduling, modestly extending the claimed applications.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the earlier favorable assessment of alternative bases: random orthonormal directions retain reasonable carry homogeneity but recover few late breakthroughs. Appendix A adds specific limitations concerning checkpoint sparsity and POS-based labeling missing interpretable skills. Appendix G also acknowledges comparable first- and second-order F1 scores.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a code-repository address, HDBSCAN hyperparameters, hyperparameter-selection rationale, filtering counts, and detailed POS-labeling rules, including the 70% threshold and two-tag restriction. Appendices D-E substantially improve documentation of the existing implementation, although the conflicting arithmetic checkpoint interval limits reproducibility.

R1.justification: V3 adds Saxe et al. on smooth aggregate learning curves and Foote et al. and Gao et al. when positioning automatic labeling. The introduction explicitly contrasts bottom-up discovery with predefined-skill analyses and relates POLCA to other unsupervised interpretability approaches; the existing research foundations remain.

P1.justification: V3 expands motivation and methodological explanations, moves limitations and English experimental details into appendices, and adds reproducibility, ethics, and AI-use statements. The main section sequence and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds comparison and hyperparameter tables, restructures homogeneity tables to include recall/F1, and expands the language-cluster panels. It redraws introductory schematics, crops arithmetic plots to 4000 iterations while retaining 10000-step training, relocates Figure 5 into the results, and adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: V1 supports hidden breakthroughs primarily through selected trajectories and carry homogeneity. V3 makes that central claim quantitatively testable and adds meaningful LCA/first-order controls, recall/F1, and direct approximation validation. Detailed clustering and labeling instructions also address important reproducibility gaps. The new 5-versus-20-iteration inconsistency is a defect, but the gains in evidential support and transparency are substantial.
